idea.title: The Turtle Town
idea.setting: a town inside a massive turtle
idea.opener: In this town, we live inside a massive turtle.
idea.premise: A whole town lives inside a giant turtle, and the Big Bad Wolf and his army hunt it down.
idea.narrator: Pip, the kid who can hear the turtle's heartbeat.
idea.twist: The turtle was never running away; it was waiting for the town to ring the bell so it could swim.
idea.teaser: The wolf was never after the town. He was after the turtle.
idea.closer: In this town, we live inside a massive turtle. And it never stops moving.

lines.text: In this town, we live inside a massive turtle.
Our streets run right down the middle of its shell.
Sunlight pours in through the cracks in the shell.
When the turtle walks, the whole town sways.
Mrs. Moss sells bread from a cart at the corner.
The kids slide down the ribs on wooden sleds.
And every night, the town sleeps to the turtle's heartbeat.
I'm Pip, and I'm the only kid who can hear it.
I keep a brass bell on a string around my neck.
Grandpa says the bell is older than the town.
Until one morning, the turtle stopped walking.
Outside, on the hill, stood the Big Bad Wolf.
He was taller than our turtle.
Behind him marched an army of soldiers.
Hundreds of them, in a long black line.
The wolf roared, and the whole shell rattled.
Then the army charged straight at our turtle.
Boom. The whole world shook.
Everyone in town ran for the middle of the shell.
I climbed up to the top of the shell and looked down.
The wolf was not after the town.
He was after the turtle.
So the whole town fought back.
The knights lined up on the edge of the shell.
The wolf stomped toward us, and the soldiers charged again.
I rang my brass bell as loud as I could.
And our turtle did what wolves never expect.
It swam.
The army stood on the shore, and the wolf fell into the sea.
The whole town cheered.
Now we live far out at sea, where no wolf can follow.
In this town, we live inside a massive turtle. And it never stops moving.
